samples.summary: Notes engine has no fail-closed writability gate: read-only mounts set only `EditorView.editable`, so every programmatic write command (including the five new list commands and `setTaskChecked`) still dispatches and syncs
samples.evidence: `initialize()` expresses read-only-ness only as `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` (editor.ts:376); `EditorState.readOnly` is never set anywhere in packages/notes. `EditorView.editable` suppresses only DOM-originated input — it does not block `view.dispatch`. The new commands dispatch unconditionally with `userEvent: 'input'` (list-commands.ts:208, list-commands.ts:290), and `note-sync.ts:64,96` forwards any non-remote `input` transaction to `store.editText()` → Yorkie. So on a viewer-role share-link mount (`shared-document.tsx:345` passes `readOnly=true`) the API surface `api.toggleBulletList() / toggleTaskList() / indentList() / outdentList()` would write to a document the visitor may only read. Today the only thing preventing that is a UI-render condition (`canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"`, notes-toolbar.tsx:241) plus the fact that `SharedNotesLayout` renders no toolbar — i.e. the gate lives outside the enforced path. This matters because the server-side backstop is off by default: `YorkieAuthController` runs in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105), returning allow for every decision it would have denied. Note the new `checkbox-input.ts:26` explicitly checks `view.state.readOnly` — a check that can never fire, because that facet is never set; only its `EditorView.editable` half does any work. Adding `EditorState.readOnly.of(readOnly)` to `buildExtensions` (or an early return in each command) would make the notes package refuse writes regardless of which caller invokes them. I could not find a currently reachable caller, hence minor rather than major.

samples.summary: The new preview-checkbox write path inherits a fail-open role check: `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` treats any unrecognised role string as writable
samples.evidence: `SharedNotesLayout` derives the only client-side authorization signal from `resolved.role === "viewer"` (shared-document.tsx:323) and forwards it to `NotesView readOnly=` (line 345) → `initialize(..., readOnly, ...)` → `onToggleTask: readOnly ? undefined : ...` (editor.ts:230-232). `ResolvedShareLink.role` is typed `role: string` (packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:17), so any value other than the exact literal `viewer` (a future `commenter`, a casing change, a missing field) mounts a *writable* preview whose checkboxes now write straight back into the shared document. Mitigating: the backend validates role against `SHARE_LINK_ROLES` at creation time (share-link.service.ts:77-79), so no non-{viewer,editor} value is expected on the wire today, and the pattern predates this change — but this diff adds a new write surface (click-to-tick anywhere on a task item) that depends on it, and the server-side check is shadow-mode-by-default. An allowlist (`role !== "editor"` → read-only) would fail closed instead.

samples.summary: `onTaskClick` never checks that the checkbox it is about to flip is enabled; the "read-only" rendering and the listener attachment are two independent copies of the same permission decision
samples.evidence: Read-only-ness of the preview is expressed twice and independently: the listener is attached only when `onToggleTask` exists (preview.ts:234), and the checkboxes are re-`disabled` post-render, also only when it is absent (preview.ts:281-285). The shared markdown-it instance is now globally configured `taskLists, { enabled: true }` (preview.ts:53), so the generated HTML is live-checkbox markup for every consumer and the read-only posture depends on a DOM patch applied after `innerHTML`. `onTaskClick` reads `checkbox.checked` and calls the callback without consulting `checkbox.disabled` (preview.ts:255-265), so if the two ever drift — a caller that passes `onToggleTask` on a read-only mount, or preview HTML reused somewhere that does not run `render()`'s disable loop — clicks become writes with no second gate. A `if (checkbox.disabled) return;` makes the two gates independent rather than duplicative. Not currently reachable: the only constructor call site is editor.ts:228, which ties the callback to `readOnly`.
